cr_data.provenance: Work was given to Mary Totto Goller in December 1915 as a gift from Georgia O'Keeffe’s aunts, Ollie and Lola Totto with whom O’Keeffe was close and who most probably had many examples of the artist’s early works.
remarks_post_1999:
This piece is not recorded in records O'Keeffe kept of her work, the Abiquiu notebooks. Barbara Buhler Lynes has examined its image characteristics, however, within the context of other watercolors O'Keeffe made as a high-school student between 1902 and 1905 that were included in the two-volume book authored by Lynes that authenticates all of O'Keeffe's known work, Georgia O'Keeffe: 
Catalogue Raisonné (Yale University Press, 1999), especially CR 7 (1903–5) and CR 15 and CR 16 (1904). 
 
The watercolor in question is unique to known works O'Keeffe completed in this period in that pastel is used to highlight forms, but the combination of mediums may have been in response to the requirements of a classroom assignment. The use of variations of one pigment to establish a background wash of grays to black is similar to CR 7 (1903–5), and black is used in both works to establish the contours of parts of the composition's forms. The use of variations of one pigment to establish backgrounds also characterizes CR 15, CR 16, and CR 17 (1904). 
 
The absence of a drawn horizontal line to separate the upper and lower parts of the composition, which appears in CR 7 (1903–5) and many of O'Keeffe's works of this period, also characterizes CR 15 and CR 16 (1904). The placement of three forms in slightly different spatial relationships along the lower edge of the composition and their overall tentativeness are similar to the forms and their placement in CR 15 and CR 16 (1904). Areas of the watercolor are not painted and appear as white highlights, a technique that is more evident in CR 15 and CR 16 (1904). The signature on the work is in the same place, made with the same medium, and the same block letters as those of CR 15 and CR 16 (1904). 
 
Technical Issues: 
The size of the work's paper support does not match that of any O’Keeffe watercolor of this period, but is fairly similar to CR 4 and CR 7 (1903–1905) although that of CR 7 is somewhat smaller. The paper support is similar in color and texture to that of CR 7. 
 
Provenance: 
Based on the information provided as well as the inscription on the work was given to Mary Totto Goller in December 1915 as a gift from Georgia O'Keeffe’s aunts, Ollie and Lola Totto with whom O’Keeffe was close and who most probably had many examples of the artist’s early works. 
 
Conclusion: 
Lynes' examination of this piece included assessing it in three areas: connoisseurship, technical qualities, and provenance. After careful analysis of these categories, and in spite of the work not being listed in O’Keeffe’s records, it is Lynes' opinion that this work was done by Georgia O’Keeffe and dates from c. 1904 with its anomalies related to it being a student work. I would include it in an addendum to the catalogue raisonné. 
 
(Source: Letter and examination by Barbara Buhler Lynes, 2012)
